judge.reason: It claims an exact infimum of 1/5, which is the same value claimed by e1.

options.counterfactual: The infimum is strictly between zero and 1/5. The sharp lower bound at 1/5 applies only when the target must also exclude pentagons, not when it merely excludes triangles.
options.approach: Separate the two target restrictions explicitly and audit the claimed lower-bound theorem. Determine whether its conclusion excludes every bounded triangle-free target or only bounded targets containing neither triangles nor pentagons.

options.counterfactual: The infimum is strictly between zero and 1/5. The sharp lower bound at 1/5 applies only when the target must also exclude pentagons, not when it merely excludes triangles.
options.approach: Develop an explicit positive lower bound using three-edge subdivisions of high-chromatic Kneser graphs and dense bipartite attachments. A homomorphism of such a subdivision into a fixed triangle-free graph would bound the chromatic number of the original Kneser graph.

options.counterfactual: The infimum is strictly between zero and 1/5. The sharp lower bound at 1/5 applies only when the target must also exclude pentagons, not when it merely excludes triangles.
options.approach: Seek an upper bound below 1/5 by allowing pentagons in the target. Construct finite labels that preserve all source edges while forbidding only triangles among target labels, rather than unnecessarily preserving the source's full odd-girth restriction.

options.counterfactual: The infimum is zero: every positive minimum-degree proportion guarantees a homomorphism to a finite triangle-free target.
options.approach: Audit the apparent positive-lower-bound construction based on subdivided Kneser graphs. Check whether its dense attachments introduce pentagons, whether the minimum-degree proportion stays uniformly positive, or whether the claimed homomorphism obstruction fails.

options.counterfactual: The infimum is zero: every positive minimum-degree proportion guarantees a homomorphism to a finite triangle-free target.
options.approach: Return to sampled neighborhoods and attempt to extend their finite labeling to uncovered vertices. Require an explicit edge-preserving map and a direct argument that a triangle among labels would force a triangle or pentagon in the source.

options.counterfactual: The infimum is zero: every positive minimum-degree proportion guarantees a homomorphism to a finite triangle-free target.
options.approach: Investigate whether a regularity partition can support a finite triangle-free target once exceptional vertices receive additional labels. Identify a precise extension lemma and prove it instead of assuming that a small exceptional set can simply be discarded.

options.counterfactual: The property holds at c = 1/5 itself, so the infimum is attained.
options.approach: Examine whether the finite-target upper bound can be made uniform as the minimum-degree proportion decreases to 1/5. A uniform bound on target size would establish the endpoint, whereas divergence alone would not disprove it.

options.counterfactual: The property holds at c = 1/5 itself, so the infimum is attained.
options.approach: Analyze structural consequences of the exact inequality delta(G) >= |V(G)|/5. Separate equality configurations from graphs with a degree margin and look for a finite collection of triangle-free targets covering the equality cases.

options.counterfactual: The property holds at c = 1/5 itself, so the infimum is attained.
options.approach: Test candidate endpoint obstructions, especially generalized Andrasfai graphs. Determine whether they all map to a fixed triangle-free graph such as the pentagon, which would prevent them from disproving attainment in this problem.
